decisions.reason: As a low-cost complementary care product for the firm’s core flooring business, it preserves a useful option while market acceptance is still too uncertain after only a short time on the market.

The maintenance oil fits closely with the installed base of wooden floors and is inexpensive to keep available, so real-options logic favors waiting for clearer demand signals rather than exiting now.

Although this care product is somewhat narrower and may overlap with other maintenance items, it still supports the core floor system and the firm has little reason to abandon it before more evidence accumulates.
A moisture-protection underlay is a technically relevant add-on to floor installations, and keeping it extends the firm’s system offering at relatively limited downside cost.

This underlay foam is somewhat more exposed to commoditization and overlap with other underlays, but the firm is still likely to keep the option open because it complements floor sales and uncertainty remains unresolved.

The oak parquet floor is strongly aligned with the firm’s core capabilities and growth strategy, and despite somewhat higher carrying costs than accessories it is too early to judge it as unsuccessful.
